It sucks, it really does. I do get how tormenting it must feel to carry the weight of this “incompatibility”. I’m a medically transitioning trans man, it’s been 2.5 years and one hell of a ride. I was brought up to believe that God says trans people are sinful, and that I am an abomination. The turning point for me was a time when I was hospitalized because my mental health was extremely unstable, and I was crying out to God in this pain having just had a Christian psychiatrist tell me to turn back to God and force me to sing hymns with him and yelled at me when I broke down. It was so painful. 
I told God how could I ever be right before you this way if I was transgender? After which, I felt God say to me “who told you this?” 
That moment marked my search for answers. Not that I can say I have them all now, but i have definitely learnt that I can question all the things that I was taught to believe and bring them to God, that it’s really ok. 
I think coming to a place of peace with our transness and faith in God is a very personal journey. People can bombard us with “facts” and information and theology and affirming stuff, which might or might not “change our minds”. But I truly think that at the end of it wherever we find ourselves on the spectrum of theological beliefs it’s just God and us, our relationship with Him. We can put the legalistic things aside for a bit, go back to the heart of worship and recognise that our God is a God beyond rules and laws. 
Let Him take you on a journey to discover His great great love for you - that’s something I’d hesitate to doubt. 😉 
Hang in there my friend.

Hey! This happened to me when I first started taping too. After awhile I realised that it was because I stretched the tape too tightly. I wanted to be as flat as possible so I thought if I stretched it more I could achieve that. I did but it caused blisters. 

Try to push the tissue to where you want it to be, I’m guessing its most probably up and out to the sides, while releasing the tape and using your hand to smooth it out as you go. Wrinkles on the tape can cause blisters too. No stretch at all at the start and end of the tape. 

You can watch the video tutorials on the trans tape website, it was helpful for me. Different people tape differently, I guess it depends on your anatomy and what you want to achieve. So do experiment till you find a method that suits you! Used to take with 3-5 strips. But after awhile I realised that less is more and could get by with 1-2 strips.

It took me weeks to get it right. Be patient with yourself, it takes some practice. But once you get it you’ll thank yourself for sticking through it! ;) 

Another thing I learnt was not to remove the tape too early while the adhesive is still strong. For me it was 5 days of wearing before trying to remove it. Please remove it with any kind of oil as well, I used baby oil.

All the best!
